staff-tags.tagline: OWNER/ADMIN/STAFF/MOD tags, computed from real permissions - not role names.
staff-tags.note: Previously broken. Rebuilt with per-patch crash isolation, plus new customization: per-tag text, colors, gradients, and visibility.
staff-tags.howItWorks:
Staff Tags looks at what a member can actually do in a server - Administrator, Manage Server, Manage Messages, Kick/Ban, and so on - and shows a small colored tag next to their name based on the highest-matching tier. It doesn't care what a role is named, so a role called "Cool Person" with Manage Messages still shows MOD. Tags appear in chat messages, the member list, the profile popout, and channel headers.

The old version of this plugin patched four separate Discord UI surfaces, and if Discord renamed even one internal component, the whole plugin's setup would throw and every tag everywhere would silently disappear. This rebuild wraps each of the four patches in its own guard, so a single broken surface degrades gracefully instead of taking the other three down with it.
features: Seven built-in tiers: Webhook, Owner, Admin, Staff, Mod, VC Mod, Chat Mod
Per-tag show/hide toggle
Custom tag text (rename "MOD" to whatever you want)
Custom solid colors with a swatch picker
Gradient tags in the member list and profile (chat tags stay solid - platform limitation, explained below)
"Use top role color" fallback when no custom color is set
staff-tags.limitations: Gradient colors only render in the member list and profile popout. Chat message tags are built from plain data passed to Discord's native row renderer, not a patchable React element, so there's no element to swap in a gradient view - they always fall back to a solid color there.

role-color-everywhere.tagline: A member's role color, applied everywhere Discord doesn't already show it.
role-color-everywhere.note: Previously broken. Ported from the original source and hardened with the same crash-isolation fix as Staff Tags.
role-color-everywhere.howItWorks: Discord already colors a message author's name by their top role - this extends that same color into places Discord leaves plain: @mentions inside message text, the "X is typing..." indicator, voice channel participant lists, and the role section headers in the member list. There's also an optional (off by default) mode that tints the message text itself toward the author's color, though that comes with a real tradeoff: it disables text selection on tinted messages, since the coloring works by wrapping the text in a link-style element.
features: Colored @mentions in chat
Colored typing indicator
Colored voice channel participant names
Colored member list role section headers
Optional message-text tinting with an adjustable strength slider (0-100)
Every surface can be toggled independently
role-color-everywhere.limitations: The member list header coloring works by patching a generic, unnamed internal component (there's no dedicated "RoleHeader" component to target), which makes it the single most fragile surface in this plugin. If a future Discord update breaks it, the other four surfaces are unaffected.

pronoun-db.tagline: Shows a user's pronouns in their profile, pulled from pronoundb.org.
pronoun-db.note: Previously broken because PronounDB shut down the API it used (HTTP 410) - migrated to their current v2 API. Requires people to have set pronouns at pronoundb.org; nothing to configure in the plugin itself.
pronoun-db.howItWorks: PronounDB is a separate, independent service (not run by Discord or Revenge) where people manually set their own pronouns once and link the profile to their Discord account. This plugin adds a "Pronouns" section near the bio on anyone's profile who has done that. Lookups are batched and cached client-side, so opening a profile for the first time may take a moment while it fetches, and re-opening the same profile later is instant.
features: Adds a native-feeling "Pronouns" section to profiles
Batches and caches lookups so scrolling through many profiles doesn't spam requests
Nothing to configure - no API key, no toggle
pronoun-db.limitations: Only shows pronouns for people who have actually created a PronounDB profile and linked their Discord account. If nobody you interact with has set one, you'll never see the section - that's expected, not a bug.

message-snippets.tagline: Save reusable text once, send it anywhere with a slash command.
message-snippets.note: Didn't exist in the Revenge/Vendetta plugin ecosystem before.
message-snippets.howItWorks: Save a name and a block of text once - server rules, an FAQ answer, your PayPal, whatever you type often - then send it in any server or DM with a single command instead of retyping or copy-pasting from notes. Snippets are stored locally on your device and sync with nothing external. Built entirely on Revenge's built-in command API rather than patching Discord's UI internals, so it doesn't carry the "might silently break on a Discord update" risk that UI-patching plugins do.
features: /snippet <name> sends the saved text as a real message
Manage everything from the plugin's settings screen: add, preview, and delete
Slash-command management too: /snippet-save, /snippet-delete, /snippet-list
No character limit beyond Discord's own message limit

commands.desc: Sends the saved snippet as a message in the current channel
Shows your saved snippet names as a toast (not posted publicly)

reminders.tagline: Quick reminders without leaving the chat you're in.
reminders.note: Didn't exist in the Revenge/Vendetta plugin ecosystem before. Only fires while Discord is running.
reminders.howItWorks: Set a reminder with a simple duration and a note, and it'll pop up as an in-app alert once it's due - no need to switch apps or set a system alarm. Reminders are checked every 15 seconds while the plugin is loaded and persist in local storage, so they survive a plugin reload, but not a fully closed app: pure-JS plugins can't schedule native OS notifications, so this can only fire while Discord's process is actually alive (foreground or backgrounded-but-running).
features: Flexible duration parsing: 10m, 2h, 1d, 30sec, 1 week, and more
See and cancel pending reminders from the plugin's settings screen
Persists across a plugin reload

commands.desc: e.g. /remind 20m Walk the dog - fires an in-app alert when it's due

reminders.limitations: Can't wake Discord up from fully closed - that needs a native OS-level scheduled notification, which isn't something a JS-only plugin has access to. If you force-close the app, pending reminders resume checking once you reopen it, but won't have fired while it was closed.

view-raw.tagline: See a message's raw JSON - searchable, syntax-highlighted, and copyable.
view-raw.note: Fork of bwlok's ViewRaw (GPLv3 - see the plugin's own LICENSE file). Fixed a crash that hit every message long-press, then rebuilt the viewer with search and syntax highlighting on top.
view-raw.howItWorks: Long-press any message and pick "View Raw" to see exactly what Discord sent for it - every field, not just the rendered text. The original plugin crashed the long-press menu on every message because it assumed a specific internal icon shape without checking it first; this fork guards that assumption and everything else in the same patch. The viewer itself was rebuilt: a search box highlights matching lines (dimming the rest, not hiding them, so you keep the structure for context), values are color-coded by type, and there are one-tap copy buttons for either just the message content or the full JSON.
features: Search box highlights matching keys/values across the whole payload
Syntax-colored JSON (strings, numbers, booleans, null all render differently)
Separate "Copy Content" and "Copy JSON" buttons
Crash fixed: no longer breaks the message long-press menu
view-raw.limitations: Licensed GPLv3 (inherited from the original), not the same terms as the rest of this repo - see plugins/view-raw/LICENSE.
